oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.neural_readout_features: One shared nn.Linear(13, 2) S3 head receives eight word one-hot coordinates, four context one-hot coordinates and one scalar local bit; there are no word-bit or context-bit interaction terms.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.binary_logit_difference: Delta(word, context, bit) = A_word + B_context + C + s * bit, where s = weight[1,12] - weight[0,12] is a single global coefficient.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.proof: With lowest-index argmax ties, identity (0,1) requires Delta(word,context,0) <= 0 and Delta(word,context,1) > 0, hence s > 0. Inverse (1,0) requires Delta(word,context,0) > 0 and Delta(word,context,1) <= 0, hence s < 0. Therefore no parameter setting of this binary affine head can implement both maps at different symbols, even at the same context. At s = 0 only constant maps are possible. Stochastic softmax also has one global monotonicity sign in the bit and cannot remove this structural restriction.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.all_frozen_r9_heads_verified: For all 16 checkpoints, evaluated all eight injected words, both local-bit values and all four public contexts under torch.no_grad. Every head has weight shape (2,13); numerical logit differences confirm its single bit coefficient, and no context table contains both identity and inverse.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.consequence: The supplied optimal unrestricted R10 decoder table is not representable by the frozen R9 affine S3 head, regardless of optimizer success or symbol relabeling. R10 remains the valid specified unrestricted EXTERNAL wire bound, not a representable frozen-neural-family optimum.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.not_established: No constrained-readout optimum or numerical expressivity-only gap was computed. Nonrepresentability of this optimal table alone does not prove that every equally optimal unrestricted table is unrepresentable; a strict risk separation for the whole affine-head family is not certified here.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.attribution: Noncapacity means not explained by the eight-word communication capacity alone; it does not mean absence of neural model-capacity restrictions. Readout representation/expressivity and held-out-context generalization must be diagnosed before attributing residual differences to learning, optimization or credit assignment. Their separate contributions are not isolated.
oracle_versus_neural_readout_expressivit.recommended_disposition: Diagnose readout representation/expressivity and held-out-context generalization before learning/credit-assignment experiments; no new training or additional variant optimization performed.

reductions.all_contexts: Permutation symmetry of iid prior and sensors yields the same bound at each public context. Stateless local heads, fresh private readings and no feedback leave no cross-tick information channel; context-dependent decoder books are permitted. Rotating this same fixed book simultaneously attains each bound, so the four-tick average remains R10; the unnormalized sum is four times R10.
reductions.at_most_eight_vs_exactly_eight: Replacing dominated policies can merge words and reduce book size. Every nonempty <=8 retained book can be padded with distinct retained policies to exactly eight without increasing risk. Duplicate decoder maps do not help. Thus exact-eight branch coverage also excludes improvement with fewer words.
reductions.deterministic_decoder: For a fixed encoder, each local action distribution contributes linearly to additive expected loss; a minimum action exists at every (consumer,word,bit,context). Alternately any legal stochastic strategy is a mixture over complete deterministic strategy tables with independent randomness; one deterministic table has no worse risk. Shared exogenous randomness independent of truth cannot beat the deterministic optimum.
reductions.deterministic_encoder: For fixed decoders, expected risk is linear in each encoder word distribution; choose a minimum-cost word per history/context.
reductions.full_history_to_counts: For fixed context and decoder book, truth posterior depends only on two-reading counts; all ordered histories sharing counts have identical conditional cost for every word. Randomly splitting such histories cannot improve the minimum word cost. All 81 count states have positive support. History order is explicitly retained in the separate frozen R9 risk calculation.
